risks.risk: Vehicle/engine fitment unknown — transmission price varies enormously by make/model, and this cannot be guessed from a casing photo alone.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the stamped part number / casing ID plate, or the vehicle (make, model, year) it was pulled from.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced at all — fitment is the primary price driver for a used transmission.

risks.risk: Mechanical condition unknown — internal gear wear, fluid contamination, or seized components are invisible from outside.
risks.proof: Video of the gearbox being rotated/shifted by hand or bench-tested, plus a photo of drained fluid condition.

risks.risk: Completeness unknown — sensors, solenoids, torque converter, or mounting brackets may be missing.
risks.proof: Multiple angle photos showing all connectors, the bellhousing face, and the torque converter (if automatic).

risks.risk: Mileage/accident or flood history unverifiable from a single shop photo.
risks.proof: Any paperwork, tags, or seller video showing where/how it was removed.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst case (unknown history, assume high risk).

proof_requests: Close-up photo of any stamped part number or ID plate on the gearbox casing.
Statement plus photo evidence of the exact vehicle make/model/year this was removed from.
Video showing the gearbox being manually shifted or bench-tested.
Additional photos from other angles showing connectors, torque converter, and bellhousing completeness.
response.reason: The part cannot even be given a worst-case price because transmission values are fitment-specific, and no make/model or part number is legible in the single photo provided.
